practice.q: Who is considered the Father of Indian Prehistory?
practice.exp: Robert Bruce Foote discovered the first Paleolithic tool in India (a handaxe) at Pallavaram near Chennai in 1863.

practice.q: Which of the following sites provides the earliest evidence of human presence in India?
practice.exp: Bori in Maharashtra provides the earliest evidence of human presence in the Indian subcontinent, dating to the Lower Paleolithic age.

practice.q: The earliest evidence of animal domestication comes from which Mesolithic sites?
practice.exp: Bagor (Rajasthan) and Adamgarh (Madhya Pradesh) provide the earliest evidence of the domestication of animals such as dogs, sheep, and goats.

practice.q: Which site provides the earliest evidence of rice cultivation in the world?
practice.exp: Recent excavations suggest rice cultivation at Lahuradewa (Sant Kabir Nagar, UP) dates back to 9000 BC, making it significantly older than Koldihwa.

practice.q: Which of the following sites is known for a massive collection of bone tools made entirely of deer antlers?
practice.exp: Chirand in Bihar is a major Neolithic site famous for its large collection of bone tools made specifically from deer antlers.

mock.q: The Narmada Human (Homo erectus) skull cap was discovered at which site?
mock.exp: The Narmada Human was discovered at Hathnora (Madhya Pradesh) by Arun Sonakia in 1982. It represents the earliest hominid fossil found in the Indian subcontinent.

mock.q: Which phase of the Stone Age is characterized by the use of 'Microliths'?
mock.exp: The Mesolithic Age is widely characterized by the use of microliths (tiny, sharp stone tools usually less than 5cm) which aided in hunting smaller prey.

mock.q: Which UP-specific site uniquely shows a continuous sequence of all three phases: Paleolithic, Mesolithic, and Neolithic?
mock.exp: The Belan Valley (Mirzapur/Prayagraj region in UP) is geographically unique for showing a continuous sequence of all three Stone Age phases.
